title: The Low Taper Fade Meme Is Still MASSIVE: The Complete Story

lines.t: In January 2024, a singer sang one sentence on a Twitch stream.
Eight days later, one of the biggest streamers on the planet walked into a barbershop because of it.
And then the internet did something even weirder. It turned the joke around, and made fun of him for loving it too much.
So how does a haircut become one of the biggest memes of 2024? It starts somewhere nobody expected. In the middle of a sad song.
Meet ericdoa. Real name Eric Lopez, a 21 year old hyperpop artist.
lines.say: Meet Eric D O A. Real name Eric Lopez, a 21 year old hyperpop artist.

lines.t: On January 5th, 2024, he went live on Twitch and freestyled for about an hour.
And this was not a joke stream. Right before the famous line, he was singing about his grandfather passing away.
The stream was getting heavy. So, to stop himself from getting too emotional, he reached for the funniest thing he could think of.
And what he came up with was this.
He later told B R Gaming that was the whole point. A way out of a moment that was getting too sad. Chat lost it.
lines.say: He later told B R Gaming that was the whole point. A way out of a moment that was getting too sad. Chat lost it.

lines.t: For almost a week, nothing happened. The YouTube upload got about 4,000 views.
Then on January 11th, a fan page called ericdoaclips posted just that one moment to TikTok.
lines.say: Then on January 11th, a fan page called Eric D O A clips posted just that one moment to TikTok.

lines.t: 1.4 million views in a single day. Over 6 million in under a week.
The line was simple. Imagine if Ninja got a low taper fade. Sung twice, like the saddest love song ever written.
The same day it blew up, people started doing what the internet does best. Making things up.
One TikToker told everyone the song was by Frank Ocean. 240,000 people watched that in a day.
Others made slideshows. Normal photos of Ninja, then a dramatic reveal of a stranger with a fresh fade.
By January 12th it had turned into a prophecy. A Fortnite video showed a wall that said, Ninja with a low taper fade solves all world problems.
Why did it work? It's short. It's sung like a heartfelt ballad, about a haircut. And it asks you to imagine something, so everyone gets to make their own version.
Then the brands showed up. The Brooklyn Nets used the sound. NFL on CBS posted, prophecy fulfilled. Rolling Loud posted, imagine no more.
ericdoa's own clip page even posted him reacting to the Brooklyn Nets using his audio.
lines.say: Eric D O A's own clip page even posted him reacting to the Brooklyn Nets using his audio.

lines.t: By January 19th, Rolling Stone had written a whole article about him, called Meet ericdoa, the reason why Ninja got a low taper fade.
lines.say: By January 19th, Rolling Stone had written a whole article about him, called Meet Eric D O A, the reason why Ninja got a low taper fade.

lines.t: But there was one person everybody was waiting on.
On January 12th, Ninja posted his first reaction. And the next day, January 13th, he did it.
He actually got the haircut.
His reveal, set to ericdoa's sound, got 5.4 million views in three days.
lines.say: His reveal, set to Eric D O A's sound, got 5.4 million views in three days.

lines.t: The internet imagined it. Ninja made it real. Story over, right?
The peak came the week of January 21st. By then it had escaped TikTok and Twitch, and people saw the line everywhere.
Not even close. Because Ninja kept talking about it. On stream. Over and over.
January 30th. Only 17 days after the haircut. A TikToker posted a clip from Ninja's stream with one caption.
Ninja is dragging the low taper fade at this point.

sc.big:
"NINJA IS DRAGGING
THE LOW TAPER FADE"

lines.t: In the clip, Ninja sings low taper fade, and then says this. You know what's crazy? Is that that low taper fade meme is like, dude, it is still massive.
And that's the funniest part of the whole story. The meme was a joke about Ninja. Then Ninja loved it so much that loving it became the new joke.
That clip pulled about 4.3 million plays.
TikTok ran with it. Edits showed Ninja still dragging the meme years in the future. As a baby. As different animals, in different lifetimes.
People made AI voice versions of the whole speech.
One edit even showed Ninja passing the haircut on to his pet bird.
And Ninja watched them. He even reacted to compilations of people making fun of him for it.
In June, someone tried to start a new one. Imagine if Tfue got a high taper fade.
It flopped. For four months. Then in October, a video saying Tfue was dragging the high taper fade got 2.3 million views in two days.
A fake meme, about a fake meme, about a real meme.

sc.big:
A FAKE MEME
ABOUT A FAKE MEME

lines.t: Then the word itself broke free.
A you know what else is massive edit in November got 5.7 million views and 872,000 likes in two months.
By January 2025 there was a parody song, a locked in Ninja remix, and a fan art trend of cartoon characters giving each other low taper fades.
Starting in February 2024, artists redrew characters from games, anime and cartoons in a barbershop, giving and getting low taper fades. Nobody was safe.
So why did this one stick, when most memes die in a week? Because it had three lives.
A sincere line, sung in a sad moment. A creator who actually did what the internet asked. And a creator who loved it so much, he became the next joke.
For ericdoa, it followed him everywhere. He's said that no matter what he posts, the comments say the same thing.
lines.say: For Eric D O A, it followed him everywhere. He's said that no matter what he posts, the comments say the same thing.

lines.t: And for Ninja, it became part of who he is online. Not just the Fortnite guy. The low taper fade guy.
And the strangest part? Even this video is proof. Because, you know what's crazy?
Which meme do you think is still massive? Tell me in the comments.
